newsitem.title: FRANCE: Counterfeit goods seized at Paris airports soar in.
newsitem.headline: Counterfeit goods seized at Paris airports soar in.

text.p: French customs said seizures of counterfeit goods at the Paris airports in 1996 rose sharply on the same period the previous year.
Counterfeit goods seized at Orly airport last year totalled 215,255 items, compared to 48,739 items in 1995.
At CDG, the number of counterfeit goods seized totalled 80,420 items compared to 32,061 items in 1995, French customs figures show.
"The vast majority of these items were designated commercial freight and were found during inspections of aircraft containers," French customs confirmed.
Orly and CDG airports accounted for 46.5 percent of the global number of counterfeit goods seized at French frontier posts in 1996 which totalled 635,542 items, compared to 27.0 percent in 1995.

French customs had devoted more resources to uncovering international trafficking networks for counterfeit goods since the introduction of tougher legislation in February 1994 and this had led to an increase in the volume of items seized.
Asia was the main region of origin for counterfeit goods destined for France or transiting French territory, in 1996, in particular, Thailand, China and Hong Kong and South Korea.

Clothing and clothing accessories was the single biggest category of counterfeit goods seized, accounting for 28 percent of the total followed by toys and games (19 percent), watches (nine percent) domestic appliances (six percent), automotive parts (five percent) and sunglasses (four percent).

A diverse range of goods including, perfumes, leather goods, audio and video cassettes, CDs, computer progammes and photographic equipment, accounted for 29 percent. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
